hints: Divide the numerator by the denominator to find the polynomial quotient $3$, then decompose the remainder fraction in partial fractions.
walkthrough:
Since the numerator and denominator have equal degree (2), divide to find the constant quotient:
$$\dfrac{6x^2 - 2x + 2}{2x^2 - x - 1} = 3 + \dfrac{(6x^2 - 2x + 2) - 3(2x^2 - x - 1)}{(x - 1)(2x + 1)}$$

Set up partial fractions for the remainder fraction:
$$\dfrac{x + 5}{(x - 1)(2x + 1)} = \dfrac{B}{x - 1} + \dfrac{C}{2x + 1}$$
Multiply through by $(x - 1)(2x + 1)$:
$$x + 5 = B(2x + 1) + C(x - 1)$$

Determine $B$ by substituting $x = 1$:
$$1 + 5 = B(2(1) + 1) + C(0)$$
$$6 = 3B \implies B = \dfrac{6}{3} = 2$$

Determine $C$ by substituting $x = -\dfrac{1}{2}$:
$$-\dfrac{1}{2} + 5 = B(0) + C\left(-\dfrac{1}{2} - 1\right)$$
$$\dfrac{9}{2} = -\dfrac{3}{2}C \implies C = \dfrac{9}{2} \times \left(-\dfrac{2}{3}\right) = -3$$

State the complete partial fractions expansion:
$$3 + \dfrac{2}{x - 1} - \dfrac{3}{2x + 1}$$
